history.period: 19th century (Old Rangji built 1844); the new Rangji temple is 20th century
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV lists town as 'Ajmer', but this temple is in Pushkar, about 15 km from Ajmer city in Ajmer district. Pushkar actually has TWO Rangji/Rangnath temples, and the CSV name is ambiguous between them: the Old Rangji (Purana Rangji ka Mandir, Shri Rangnath Venugopal) near Varah Ghat, built in 1844 by Seth Puranmal Ganeriwal of Lakshmangarh in Shekhawati, and the New Rangji (Naya Rangji) near the Pushkar bus stand at the town entrance. The coordinates below are for the geocoded 'Rangji Temple' at Badi Basti on Ajmer Road - the town-entrance site. Both temples are Sri Vaishnava (Ramanuja) temples of the Paushkara branch, remarkable for their tall South Indian-style gopurams in the Rajasthani desert, blending Dravidian towers with Rajasthani jharokhas and chhatris. The old temple's presiding deity is a four-armed Venugopala (Krishna) in black Kadappa stone from Tamil Nadu, flanked by Rukmini and Satyabhama, and its outer parikrama carries frescoes of Krishna Leela, Ramayana and Sagarmanthan. Leather articles are traditionally not allowed inside. Regular free evening classical-music concerts are reported at the old temple (verify).

name: Shri Rangnath Swami Temple
town: Pushkar (CSV town 'Ajmer' is approximate - the temple is in Pushkar town, Ajmer district)
town_description: Pushkar, about 15 km northwest of Ajmer, is one of Hinduism's oldest pilgrimage towns - famed for its sacred lake ringed by ghats, the rare Brahma Temple, and the annual Pushkar Camel Fair. It draws pilgrims, foreign travellers and camel traders, and is ringed by hills including the Savitri temple hill.

travel.road: On Ajmer Road at the entrance to Pushkar town; regular buses and taxis from Ajmer (verify).
